newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm 0.79 pct to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm 0.79 pct to new record close.

text.p: Istanbul shares continued to post gains on Thursday as the market targeted new records in the index amid selective buys fuelled by first half company profit prospects, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 2,050, up 16 points, or 0.79 percent from Wednesday and compared to a previous record of 2,043 on July 14. But it was down from 2,065, the trading record it equalled in early trade.
Daily trade volume rose by 18.5 percent to 24.95 trillion lira ($153 million) from Wednesday's 21.05 trillion ($129 million).

"There was profit taking in the second session which was healthy when considering the current high levels. The market did not focus on a few shares and there was also activity in low priced shares" said Gokhan Kolay from Polen Securities.

"The index may continue its rise as long as activity continues to spread around in the market and foreing investors' interest persists," he said, adding that technically, the market's index target was 3,000 points for the year end.

Some brokers said the current volume was not sufficient to carry the market further up and deeper activity was needed in locomotives such as bluechip shares of state, energy or financial sector shares.
The most heavily traded stock of the day was again largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli which made up 8.2 percent of the total turnover.
